answer: A claimant grinds pigment from their registered relic stone and paints a tide mark on a haven pier post at low tide; the pigment fades at a known rate, so its shade proves when the mark was made. Two haven wardens compare the mark against the fading chart within three days and check the pigment's grain against the relic register. A mark too fresh, too faded, or painted twice voids the season, burns a 220-credit stake, and bars the pier two seasons. Forging 1,000 false marks means grinding 1,000 relics and painting 1,000 pier posts by hand, while one honest claimant paints one.
